context: Sable Creek Health's ICU vitals-rounding tablets are provisioned per Nursing Informatics SOP 4.2 to remain logged in under a shared unit-function service account, not an individual clinician credential, for rapid vitals entry across multiple patients per shift. Audit review of tablet 4W-TAB-06 showed the account logged in continuously for a 12-hour shift on 2026-09-13, with 5 different staff badges tapping an RFID-based per-entry attribution layer that logs the actual entering clinician separately from the session account. All 118 vitals entries during the shift carried a valid per-entry attribution matching a scheduled staff member; no entries were made outside scheduled staff hours.

choice_questions.prompt: Does this shared-login pattern violate access-control policy?
candidates: Yes, shared logins are never permitted for any clinical device
No, it matches the documented shared-device SOP with per-entry attribution
Yes, because five different people used one login with no attribution
It cannot be determined without more information

choice_questions.prompt: How is individual accountability maintained despite the shared session account?
candidates: It is not maintained; entries are anonymous
A separate RFID-based per-entry attribution layer
Each staff member re-logs in for every single entry
Supervisors manually reconcile entries weekly from memory

noul_queries.assertion: This pattern matches a documented, sanctioned SOP.

context: Larkspur Health Network's patient-portal WAF logged 620 failed login attempts across 340 distinct patient-facing accounts between 2026-09-17 14:00-16:00, originating from a rotating pool of roughly 85 residential-proxy IP addresses consistent with a credential-stuffing tool using a breached-password list. 11 attempts succeeded before rate-limiting and anomaly-detection triggered a step-up MFA challenge for the affected accounts. Of the 11 successful logins, 4 proceeded to view billing/insurance pages, 0 reached medical-records tabs before session termination. Affected accounts forced to password reset; breach-notification threshold review underway for the 11 accessed accounts.

choice_questions.prompt: What signature most clearly identifies this as credential stuffing rather than normal login failures?
candidates: A single user forgetting their password twice
A scheduled password-expiration reminder causing simultaneous resets
A large volume of failed logins across many accounts from a rotating residential-proxy IP pool
One IP address failing to log into one account repeatedly

choice_questions.prompt: How many of the successful logins reached medical-records tabs before termination?

noul_queries.assertion: All login attempts originated from a single fixed IP address.
Some accounts were successfully accessed before detection.
Medical-records content was reached during the compromised sessions.

context: Marrowgate Medical Center's identity-governance review found agency-nurse credential RN-TEMP-2249 (contract ended 2026-08-15, badge deactivated same day per offboarding checklist) was used to log into the EHR from an external home-ISP IP address on 2026-08-24, nine days after contract end, viewing 22 patient charts across two units the nurse had never been assigned to during her contract. VPN access had not been separately revoked due to a gap between the staffing agency's offboarding notice and IT's VPN-deprovisioning queue. Charts viewed had no billing, scheduling, or continuity-of-care justification. Access ticket opened, VPN credential force-revoked, agency contract flagged for review.

choice_questions.prompt: What allowed this post-termination access to occur?
candidates: The EHR does not track termination dates at all
The nurse was rehired the same week under a new contract
A gap between offboarding notice and VPN-credential deprovisioning left remote access active
IT intentionally left access open for a transition period with approval

choice_questions.prompt: Were the charts viewed within the nurse's prior assigned units?
candidates: No, different units entirely
Yes, her assigned units

noul_queries.assertion: The badge/EHR account was deactivated on the contract end date.
VPN access was also revoked on the contract end date.
There was a documented care-related reason for viewing these charts.
